articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities for Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Activities, Issues New Cuba Sanctions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today targeting entities involved in cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations. This action aims to disrupt illicit networks that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.

In addition to these designations, OFAC also implemented new sanctions related to Cuba. These measures are part of the ongoing U.S. policy to address human rights concerns and support democratic aspirations in Cuba.

A Cuba-related determination was also published, providing further details on the scope and implications of the new sanctions. The Treasury Department continues to monitor and adapt its sanctions programs to effectively counter evolving threats.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-related Designations, Amends Venezuela General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting individuals and entities connected to Iran. These actions are part of a broader strategy to counter Iran's destabilizing activities in the region and its proliferation of weapons.

Alongside the new designations, OFAC also updated certain Iran-related listings to ensure the accuracy and effectiveness of its sanctions program. An Iran-related OFAC Alert was published, providing guidance to the public on potential risks and compliance obligations.

Furthermore, an amended Venezuela-related General License was issued, along with a new Frequently Asked Question, to provide clarity and facilitate certain transactions involving Venezuela. This amendment reflects ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy in the region.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment aims to provide further clarity and potentially expand the scope of authorized activities under the existing sanctions program.

The specific details of the amendments are available on the Treasury Department's website. Entities and individuals engaging in Iran-related transactions are advised to review the updated guidance to ensure compliance.
This action reflects OFAC's ongoing efforts to refine and adjust its sanctions policies in response to evolving circumstances and to ensure humanitarian and other authorized activities can proceed.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Linked to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting entities associated with North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These actions are part of the U.S. government's commitment to addressing threats to international peace and security.

The North Korea designations aim to counter the regime's illicit activities, including its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. The Democratic Republic of the Congo-related designations address human rights abuses and corruption within the region.
These measures underscore the U.S. resolve to hold accountable those who engage in destabilizing behavior and violate international norms.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Reaches Settlement Agreement with OFAC
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. The settlement resolves apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.

Details of the settlement, including the specific violations and the agreed-upon penalty, are available on the OFAC website. This action highlights the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.

OFAC continues to emphasize that companies are responsible for ensuring their operations do not violate U.S. sanctions laws, and voluntary self-disclosure and cooperation are considered in enforcement actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update provides further clarification and guidance for financial institutions and other entities subject to OFAC regulations.

The amendments aim to assist in understanding and complying with reporting requirements related to blocked property and rejected transactions. Adherence to these guidelines is crucial for maintaining an effective sanctions compliance program.
OFAC regularly updates its FAQs to address common questions and provide timely information on its policies and procedures, reflecting the dynamic nature of sanctions implementation.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran Sanctions, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new Iran-related designations, continuing its pressure on the Iranian regime. These actions target specific entities and individuals deemed to be involved in activities that contravene U.S. foreign policy objectives.

In a separate development, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. These removals indicate a reassessment of the sanctioned parties' activities or a change in policy.

Additionally, new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses were issued, alongside amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing updated guidance on permissible activities under these sanctions programs. This reflects the ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations, Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA). These designations aim to combat the theft of American intellectual property and protect U.S. economic interests.

The PAIPA designations target individuals and entities involved in activities that compromise intellectual property rights. This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to safeguarding innovation and technological advantage.

Associated General Licenses were also issued to provide guidance on permissible activities and to mitigate unintended consequences of these new designations. Stakeholders are advised to review these licenses carefully for compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). This update provides further clarification and adjusts the scope of authorized transactions involving Venezuela.

The amendment aims to facilitate certain humanitarian or other permissible activities while maintaining pressure on the Maduro regime. Entities engaging in Venezuela-related transactions should review the updated guidance.
OFAC continues to adapt its sanctions programs to address the evolving situation in Venezuela and to ensure that U.S. policy objectives are met effectively.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran and Cuba Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new Iran-related designations and a new Cuba designation. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter threats posed by these regimes to U.S. national security and foreign policy.

The Iran designations target entities and individuals involved in illicit activities, while the Cuba designation reinforces existing sanctions aimed at promoting democratic change. These measures underscore the U.S. commitment to holding these governments accountable.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions. These resources provide guidance to the public on the scope of the sanctions and permissible transactions.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined $1,529,685 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has been assessed a civil monetary penalty of $1,529,685 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This penalty is for apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.

The enforcement action underscores the importance of comprehensive sanctions compliance programs for companies engaged in international business. OFAC continues to actively pursue entities that fail to adhere to U.S. sanctions laws.
Companies are reminded to conduct thorough due diligence and implement robust internal controls to prevent violations, particularly when dealing with high-risk jurisdictions or entities.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Penalized $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Breaches
body: Bank of America, N.A. has been assessed a civil monetary penalty of $11,662,930 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This significant penalty is for apparent violations of various U.S. sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

This enforcement action is part of a coordinated effort by the Treasury Department, with FinCEN assessing a $1.2 billion penalty and the OCC imposing a $750 million civil money penalty for widespread BSA/AML failures.

The violations highlight the critical need for financial institutions to maintain robust sanctions compliance programs and to address deficiencies in transaction monitoring, customer due diligence, and suspicious activity reporting.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Fined $175,015 by OFAC
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has been assessed a civil monetary penalty of $175,015 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The penalty is for apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.

This enforcement action serves as a reminder to logistics and shipping companies of their obligations to comply with U.S. sanctions laws. Due diligence in international shipments is crucial to avoid facilitating prohibited transactions.
OFAC continues to enforce its regulations across various industries to prevent sanctioned entities from accessing the U.S. financial system or engaging in prohibited trade.

articles.headline: Individual Penalized $1,427,230 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: An individual has been assessed a civil monetary penalty of $1,427,230 by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This penalty is for apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.
This enforcement action highlights that individuals, not just corporations, can be held accountable for sanctions breaches. Personal responsibility in adhering to U.S. sanctions laws is paramount.
OFAC continues to pursue enforcement actions against individuals who engage in prohibited transactions or facilitate activities on behalf of sanctioned entities.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
